t:
Section 3 of the Maritime Academy Act of 1958 (46 U.S.C. 1382) is amended by inserting a new subsection (c) to read as follows:

“(c) In any case where the Secretary has not, prior to the enactment of this subsection, furnished a suitable vessel to a State as authorized by subsection (a) of this section, the Secretary may, in lieu of furnishing such a vessel, repair, recondition and equip (including all apparel, charts, books, and instruments of navigation) as necessary, a vessel which is owned by a State on the date of enactment of this subsection, for use as a training vessel for a maritime academy or college meeting the requirements of this Act.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that because a State is mentioned, this is federal-state coordination. But the provision only authorizes the Secretary to repair and equip a State-owned training vessel instead of furnishing a federal one, which is a form of assistance to the State. It does not require consultation, a hearing, comment, rulemaking, an advisory body, or any right to sue before a federal decision is made.
fable.s: the Secretary may, in lieu of furnishing such a vessel, repair, recondition and equip (including all apparel, charts, books, and instruments of navigation) as necessary, a vessel which is owned by a State

qwen_block.w: This section grants the Secretary of the Navy (or relevant Secretary) the discretionary authority to repair or equip a state-owned vessel instead of providing a new one. It does not require the Secretary to consult with the state, hold a public hearing, or involve any outside party in the decision-making process. The interaction described is a unilateral executive action regarding the provision of equipment, not a participatory process involving outside entities in a federal decision.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary may, in lieu of furnishing such a vessel, repair, recondition and equip... a vessel which is owned by a State

opus.w: This provision lets the Secretary repair and equip a State-owned vessel for use as a training ship instead of providing a federal one. A State is named, which makes it tempting to call this participation. But the State only receives assistance, which is like a benefit. The section requires no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue before the Secretary decides.
opus.s: the Secretary may, in lieu of furnishing such a vessel, repair, recondition and equip (including all apparel, charts, books, and instruments of navigation) as necessary, a vessel which is owned by a State

qwen_chat.w: This section grants the Secretary of the Navy the authority to repair and equip a state-owned vessel. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from the State or any other outside party before making this decision. The interaction is purely operational and unilateral on the part of the federal agency, lacking the procedural elements of participation defined in the instructions.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary may, in lieu of furnishing such a vessel, repair, recondition and equip (including all apparel, charts, books, and instruments of navigation) as necessary, a vessel which is owned by a State
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Secretary interacts with a State-owned vessel, this involves coordination with an outside entity. However, the text describes a unilateral action by the Secretary (repairing/equipping a vessel) rather than a process of consultation, advisory input, or joint decision-making with the State. The State is the owner of the asset, but the statute does not require the State's input or participation in the decision to repair or equip the vessel; it merely grants the Secretary the authority to do so.
